description: NFUpdate constraints extracted from normative SHALL/MUST statements in the provided section.

constraints.statement: For NF Profile complete replacement, the NF Service Consumer shall issue an HTTP PUT request to the resource URI representing the NF Instance.
evidence: To perform a complete replacement of the NF Profile of a given NF Instance, the NF Service Consumer shall issue an HTTP PUT request
The NF Service Consumer shall send a PUT request to the resource URI representing the NF Instance.
constraints.why_interesting: This is the required HTTP method and target resource for the complete-replacement variant.

constraints.statement: For NF Profile complete replacement, the PUT request body shall contain a representation of the NF Instance to be completely replaced in the NRF.
evidence: The content of the PUT request shall contain a representation of the NF Instance to be completely replaced in the NRF.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required request payload rule that can be checked by API validation.

constraints.statement: On successful NF Profile complete replacement, the NRF shall return 200 OK.
evidence: On success, "200 OK" shall be returned
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required success status code for the PUT operation.

constraints.statement: On successful NF Profile complete replacement, the PUT response body shall contain the representation of the replaced resource.
evidence: the content of the PUT response shall contain the representation of the replaced resource
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required response-body behavior that can be asserted in tests.

constraints.statement: If NF Profile complete replacement fails due to errors in encoding the NFProfile JSON object, the NRF shall return 400 Bad Request with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If the update of the NF instance fails at the NRF due to errors in the encoding of the NFProfile JSON object, the NRF shall return "400 Bad Request" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This defines a specific client-error status and error payload for malformed input.

constraints.statement: If NF Profile complete replacement fails due to NRF internal errors, the NRF shall return 500 Internal Server Error with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If the update of the NF instance fails at the NRF due to NRF internal errors, the NRF shall return "500 Internal Server Error" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the server-error behavior for internal failures.

constraints.statement: If NF Profile complete replacement is redirected, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code with a Location header pointing to another NRF service instance endpoint.
evidence: In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return 3xx status code, which shall contain a Location header with an URI pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a testable redirect requirement including a mandatory header.

constraints.statement: For NF Profile partial update, the NF Service Consumer shall issue an HTTP PATCH request to the resource URI representing the NF Instance.
evidence: To perform a partial update of the NF Profile of a given NF Instance, the NF Service Consumer shall issue an HTTP PATCH request
The NF Service Consumer shall send a PATCH request to the resource URI representing the NF Instance.
constraints.why_interesting: This is the required HTTP method and target resource for the partial-update variant.

constraints.statement: For NF Profile partial update, the PATCH request body shall contain the list of add/delete/replace operations to be applied to the NF Profile.
evidence: The content of the PATCH request shall contain the list of operations (add/delete/replace) to be applied to the NF Profile of the NF Instance
constraints.why_interesting: This is a concrete request-body requirement for patch semantics.

constraints.statement: For NF Profile partial update, all operations specified by the PATCH request body shall be executed atomically.
evidence: all the operations specified by the PATCH request body shall be executed atomically
constraints.why_interesting: This is an observable transactional rule that can be tested by inducing partial failure.

constraints.statement: For NF Profile partial update, the NF Service Consumer should include an If-Match header carrying the latest entity-tag received from the NRF.
evidence: The NF Service Consumer should include a "If-Match" HTTP header carrying the latest entity-tag received from NRF for the NF profile to which the PATCH document shall be applied.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a conditional request recommendation, but not a SHALL/MUST rule, so it is not included as a normative constraint.

constraints.statement: On successful NF Profile partial update, the NRF shall return 204 No Content when all update operations are accepted.
evidence: On success, if all update operations are accepted by the NRF, "204 No Content" should be returned
constraints.why_interesting: This is the primary success status for PATCH, though expressed as SHOULD rather than SHALL.

constraints.statement: If the NF Instance identified by nfInstanceID is not found during NF Profile partial update, the NRF shall return 404 Not Found with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If the NF Instance, identified by the "nfInstanceID", is not found in the list of registered NF Instances in the NRF's database, the NRF shall return "404 Not Found" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a specific not-found error condition for PATCH.

constraints.statement: If the If-Match header is received with an entity tag different from the NRF entity-tag for the target NF instance, the NRF shall return 412 Precondition Failed with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If "If-Match" header is received with an entity tag different from the entity-tag in NRF for NF profile of the target NF instance, the NRF shall return "412 Precondition Failed" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a precise conditional-update failure rule.

constraints.statement: If no precondition was defined in the request and another conflict is detected during NF Profile partial update, the NRF shall return 409 Conflicting with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If no precondition was defined in the request and another confliction has been detected (e.g. to change value of a non-existing IE), the NRF shall return "409 Conflicting" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This defines conflict handling when no conditional header is present.

constraints.statement: The NRF shall allow updating Vendor-Specific attributes in the NF Profile of a registered NF Instance.
evidence: The NRF shall allow updating Vendor-Specific attributes (see 3GPP TS 29.500 [4], clause 6.6.3) that may exist in the NF Profile of a registered NF Instance.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a capability requirement that can be tested by attempting to update vendor-specific fields.

constraints.statement: For Shared Data complete replacement, the NF Service Consumer shall issue an HTTP PUT request to the resource URI representing the Shared Data.
evidence: To perform a complete replacement of the Shared Data, the NF Service Consumer shall issue an HTTP PUT request
The NF Service Consumer shall send a PUT request to the resource URI representing the Shared Data.
constraints.why_interesting: This is the required HTTP method and target resource for shared-data replacement.

constraints.statement: For Shared Data complete replacement, the PUT request body shall contain a representation of the Shared Data to be completely replaced in the NRF.
evidence: The content of the PUT request shall contain a representation of the Shared Data to be completely replaced in the NRF.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required request payload rule for shared-data replacement.

constraints.statement: On successful Shared Data complete replacement, the NRF shall return 200 OK or 204 No Content.
evidence: On success, either "200 OK" shall be returned, the content of the PUT response shall contain the representation of the replaced resource, or "204 No Content" shall be returned.
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the allowed success statuses for shared-data PUT.

constraints.statement: If Shared Data complete replacement fails due to errors in encoding the SharedData JSON object, the NRF shall return 400 Bad Request with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If the update of the Shared Data fails at the NRF due to errors in the encoding of the SharedData JSON object, the NRF shall return "400 Bad Request" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a specific client-error condition for malformed shared-data input.

constraints.statement: If Shared Data complete replacement is not authorized with write access to the requesting NF, the NRF shall return 403 Forbidden with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If the Shared Data is not authorized with write access to the requesting NF ... the NRF shall return "403 Forbidden" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This is an authorization failure that can be tested by using an unauthorized NF.

constraints.statement: If Shared Data complete replacement fails due to NRF internal errors, the NRF shall return 500 Internal Server Error with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If the update of the Shared Data fails at the NRF due to NRF internal errors, the NRF shall return "500 Internal Server Error" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the server-error behavior for shared-data replacement.

constraints.statement: If Shared Data complete replacement is redirected, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code with a Location header pointing to another NRF service instance endpoint.
evidence: In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return 3xx status code, which shall contain a Location header with an URI pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a testable redirect requirement including a mandatory header.

constraints.statement: For Shared Data partial update, the NF Service Consumer shall issue an HTTP PATCH request to the resource URI representing the Shared Data.
evidence: To perform a partial update of the Shared Data, the NF Service Consumer shall issue an HTTP PATCH request
The NF Service Consumer shall send a PATCH request to the resource URI representing the Shared Data.
constraints.why_interesting: This is the required HTTP method and target resource for shared-data partial update.

constraints.statement: For Shared Data partial update, the PATCH request body shall contain the list of add/delete/replace operations to be applied to the Shared Data.
evidence: The content of the PATCH request shall contain the list of operations (add/delete/replace) to be applied to the Shared Data
constraints.why_interesting: This is a concrete request-body requirement for shared-data patch semantics.

constraints.statement: For Shared Data partial update, all operations specified by the PATCH request body shall be executed atomically.
evidence: all the operations specified by the PATCH request body shall be executed atomically
constraints.why_interesting: This is an observable transactional rule that can be tested by inducing partial failure.

constraints.statement: On successful Shared Data partial update, the NRF shall return 204 No Content when all update operations are accepted.
evidence: On success, if all update operations are accepted by the NRF, "204 No Content" should be returned
constraints.why_interesting: This is the primary success status for shared-data PATCH, though expressed as SHOULD rather than SHALL.

constraints.statement: If the Shared Data identified by sharedDataId is not found during partial update, the NRF shall return 404 Not Found with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If the Shared Data, identified by the "sharedDataId", is not found in the NRF's database, the NRF shall return "404 Not Found" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a specific not-found error condition for shared-data PATCH.

constraints.statement: If the Shared Data is not authorized with write access to the requesting NF during partial update, the NRF shall return 403 Forbidden with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If the Shared Data is not authorized with write access to the requesting NF ... the NRF shall return "403 Forbidden" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This is an authorization failure that can be tested by using an unauthorized NF.

constraints.statement: If Shared Data partial update is redirected, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code with a Location header pointing to another NRF service instance endpoint.
evidence: In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return 3xx status code, which shall contain a Location header with an URI pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a testable redirect requirement including a mandatory header.

constraints.statement: If the If-Match header is received with an entity tag different from the NRF entity-tag for the target NF instance during Shared Data partial update, the NRF shall return 412 Precondition Failed with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If "If-Match" header is received with an entity tag different from the entity-tag in NRF for NF profile of the target NF instance, the NRF shall return "412 Precondition Failed" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a conditional-update failure rule, though the text appears to reference NF profile terminology in the shared-data subsection.

constraints.statement: If no precondition was defined in the request and another conflict is detected during Shared Data partial update, the NRF shall return 409 Conflicting with ProblemDetails.
evidence: If no precondition was defined in the request and another confliction has been detected (e.g. to change value of a non-existing IE), the NRF shall return "409 Conflicting" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: This defines conflict handling when no conditional header is present.

constraints.statement: Each NF that has previously registered in NRF shall contact the NRF periodically by invoking the NFUpdate service operation.
evidence: Each NF that has previously registered in NRF shall contact the NRF periodically (heart-beat), by invoking the NFUpdate service operation, in order to show that the NF is still operative.
constraints.why_interesting: This is the normative heartbeat requirement for registered NFs.

constraints.statement: The NRF shall return the deployment-specific heart-beat interval to the NF Service Consumer as a result of a successful registration.
evidence: The time interval at which the NRF shall be contacted is deployment-specific, and it is returned by the NRF to the NF Service Consumer as a result of a successful registration.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required information flow that can be checked after registration.

constraints.statement: When the NRF detects that a given NF has not updated its profile for a configurable amount of time longer than the heart-beat interval, the NRF shall change the NF status to SUSPENDED.
evidence: When the NRF detects that a given NF has not updated its profile for a configurable amount of time (longer than the heart-beat interval), the NRF changes the status of the NF to SUSPENDED
constraints.why_interesting: This is a state-transition rule triggered by missed heartbeats.

constraints.statement: When the NRF changes an NF status to SUSPENDED, it shall consider that the NF and its services can no longer be discovered by other NFs via the NFDiscovery service.
evidence: considers that the NF and its services can no longer be discovered by other NFs via the NFDiscovery service
constraints.why_interesting: This is an externally observable discovery restriction after suspension.

constraints.statement: When the NRF changes an NF status to SUSPENDED, it shall notify subscribed NFs that the NF status has changed to SUSPENDED.
evidence: The NRF notifies NFs subscribed to receiving notifications of changes of the NF Profile that the NF status has been changed to SUSPENDED.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required notification behavior after state change.

constraints.statement: If the NRF modifies the heart-beat interval value of a currently registered NF instance, it shall return the new value in the response of the next periodic heart-beat interaction received from that NF.
evidence: If the NRF modifies the heart-beat interval value of a given NF instance currently registered ... it shall return the new value to the registered NF in the response of the next periodic heart-beat interaction received from that NF
constraints.why_interesting: This is a specific update-propagation rule for heartbeat interval changes.

constraints.statement: Until the next periodic heart-beat interaction after a heart-beat interval change, the NRF shall apply the heart-beat check procedure according to the original interval value.
evidence: until then, the NRF shall apply the heart-beat check procedure according to the original interval value.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a temporal rule governing behavior between configuration change and next heartbeat.

constraints.statement: For Heart-Beat, the NF Service Consumer shall send a PATCH request to the resource URI representing the NF Instance.
evidence: The NF Service Consumer shall send a PATCH request to the resource URI representing the NF Instance.
constraints.why_interesting: This is the required HTTP method and target resource for heartbeat.

constraints.statement: For Heart-Beat, the PATCH request body shall contain a replace operation on the nfStatus attribute of the NF Profile.
evidence: The content of the PATCH request shall contain a "replace" operation on the "nfStatus" attribute of the NF Profile of the NF Instance
constraints.why_interesting: This is a concrete request-body requirement for heartbeat.

constraints.statement: For Heart-Beat, the nfStatus value shall be set to REGISTERED or UNDISCOVERABLE.
evidence: and set it to the value "REGISTERED" or "UNDISCOVERABLE".
constraints.why_interesting: This constrains the allowed heartbeat status values.

constraints.statement: For Heart-Beat, the NF Service Consumer shall not include an If-Match header if the request is not modifying any attribute in the NF profile.
evidence: The NF Service Consumer shall not include "If-Match" HTTP header in the Heart-Beat request if the request is not modifying any attribute in the NF profile.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a forbidden header condition that can be tested directly.

constraints.statement: On successful Heart-Beat, the NRF should return 204 No Content.
evidence: On success, the NRF should return "204 No Content"
constraints.why_interesting: This is the primary success status for heartbeat, though expressed as SHOULD rather than SHALL.

constraints.statement: For Heart-Beat, the NRF shall not generate a new entity tag for the NF profile if no attribute is modified.
evidence: The NRF shall not generate a new entity tag for the NF profile in Heart-Beat operation if no attribute is modified.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a testable idempotency/versioning rule for no-op heartbeats.
